risk_if_not_implemented: Without Limit Network Connections, adversaries may move laterally, exfiltrate data or reach systems that should have been isolated from untrusted networks. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, no risk is rated Likely; risks rated Possible include Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Reduced Operational Productivity (R-BC-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_1.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Limit Network Connections (NET-03.1) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Software Firewall
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize host-based firewall software, or a similar technology, on all endpoint devices, where technically feasible.
compensating_control_2.justification: Software Firewall (END-07) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Limit Network Connections (NET-03.1) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
